files.onlyFilesOpenable: Only files can be opened in an application.
files.openInAppHelp: Launch an installed app with this file. The file is copied into the session's storage and opened in the app.

launch.uploadStorage: Upload a file to shared storage

launch.subtitle: The app will launch without opening a file. Check "Open file on launch" to pick one.
launch.sessionNamePlaceholder: Appears in the window title and session list

howto.title: How to Use Vreckan
howto.intro: A quick guide to the main things you can do in Vreckan.
howto.item1Body: Open the Apps tab, pick an application, set your launch options (home directory, language, GPU, …) and click Launch. Your isolated session opens in a new tab.
howto.item2Lead: Open a file in an app
howto.item2Body: In the Files tab, select a file and choose “Open in app” to launch it directly in the application of your choice.
howto.item3Body: Create and delete home directories (from the launch options or the Files tab) to keep your files across sessions.
howto.item4Body: Tick “Save these launch options” in the launch dialog to pin a preset for a file type or for all URLs. Manage presets under Pinned.
howto.item5Body: In the Admin tab you can manage users, admins, groups, apps, templates, volume mounts and backups.

accounts.heading: Accounts
accounts.addHelp: Create a new account. Tick "Admin" to make it an administrator.
accounts.accessHelp: Assign roles, direct permissions, and group memberships. The account's effective access is the union of all three (the most permissive wins).
accounts.passwordHelp: Sets the web-login password for {username}. It takes effect immediately — they can use it to sign in to the web UI.
accounts.toastPasswordTooShort: Password must be at least 8 characters
accounts.editAdminLockedTitle: The bootstrap admin account cannot be demoted.

groups.heading: Groups
groups.ssoAdminTitle: In the admin SSO list (grants admin)

gs.heading: Global Settings
gs.help: Server-wide settings. The per-setting base-layer defaults (the template schema) are edited below on this page, and the SSO admin groups are managed on the {groups} page.
gs.gpuHelp: Fallback GPU for launches where the user doesn't pick one. Apps that don't support the GPU type are unaffected.

sso.heading: SSO / OIDC
sso.help: Connect Vreckan to an OpenID Connect provider (e.g. authentik). Discovery is fetched from {issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration. A value saved here overrides the VRECKAN_OIDC_* environment; the badge on each field shows its current source.
sso.groupMappingHelp: On each SSO login a user is joined to a Vreckan group for every provider group they're in. Only the groups listed below get roles auto-assigned; any other (newly observed) group starts with no permissions until you grant them on the {groups} page.
sso.adminGroupsHelp: Members are auto-promoted to Vreckan admin (grants the admin role).
sso.userGroupsHelp: Members get the built-in user role. The first of these a user belongs to becomes their primary group.

certificates.heading: Certificates
certificates.help: Issue and renew Let’s Encrypt certificates with certbot. When disabled, the server uses a self-signed certificate.
certificates.domainsHelp: Comma-separated domain(s) to issue certificates for.
certificates.authHelp: DNS-01 works behind a reverse proxy; HTTP-01 requires the ACME server to reach your domain over HTTP.
certificates.stagingHelp: Test certificates from the Let’s Encrypt staging server (no production rate limits).
certificates.emailHelp: Account email for Let’s Encrypt. Optional when using a Cloudflare API token.
certificates.tokenOptional: Leave blank to keep the current token
certificates.tokenHelp: A Cloudflare API token with Zone.DNS edit permission for the domain’s zone.
certificates.checkHoursHelp: How often to check whether the certificate needs renewing.
certificates.renewBeforeHelp: Renew the certificate when it expires within this many days.
certificates.noCert: No certificate found. Enable Let’s Encrypt and issue one, or the server is using a self-signed certificate.

mounts.heading: Volume Mounts
mounts.addHelp: Bind a directory from the Docker host into app containers. Container paths are relative to the user's home directory inside the container.

apps.heading: Apps
apps.installFromStoreHelp: Pick a store to browse available apps, then choose one to install.
apps.allUpToDate: All apps are up to date
apps.updatesStarted: Started updating {count} app(s) — progress is shown in the table
apps.somePullsFailed: Some updates failed — check the table
apps.pullStarted: Pull started — progress is shown in the table
apps.pullTimedOut: Pull timed out — check back later
apps.installHelp: Installs the app and downloads its container image. The download runs in the background — progress is shown below.
apps.noOneSelected: No one is selected — this app will be hidden from and unusable by everyone.
apps.urlEnvVarHelp: The environment variable this app reads the launch URL from. Upstream linuxserver images use <APP>_CLI — e.g. CHROME_CLI for Chrome, FIREFOX_CLI for Firefox. Leave empty if the app doesn't open a URL.

tpl.appTemplatesHelp: Templates define the environment variables passed to session containers. Only values that differ from the defaults are stored.
tpl.baseLayerHelp: The template schema: the environment variables offered to app templates and their default (base-layer) values. Every launch starts from these defaults; per-app templates and per-launch choices override them. "docker" settings become container run-options instead of environment variables. An empty value lets the image's built-in default apply. Changes apply to new launches.
tpl.dockerHelp: These settings override the default container configuration. Use with caution and only if you know what you are doing.
tpl.heading: Templates
tpl.label: Label
tpl.namePlaceholder: Enter a name for the new template
tpl.webrtcHelp: Sessions stream over WebSockets by default. Setting any STUN, TURN, Cloudflare or public IP value below, or choosing WebRTC mode, switches the container to WebRTC with dual mode enabled so users can still fall back to WebSockets.
tpl.advancedWarning: Changes to these settings can break app launches, so it is recommended to make a backup before changing anything on this page.

sessions.heading: Sessions
sessions.outOfDate: Out of date — a newer image is available
sessions.recreateTitle: Recreate this session from the latest image (the app briefly goes offline)
sessions.sendFileTitle: Upload a file from your computer into this session

backup.heading: Backup
backup.createHelp: Creates a tar.gz of the application configuration in /data/backups. Restoring re-applies it to the running server without a restart.
backup.restoreFromFileHelp: Upload a previously downloaded backup tar.gz to restore it. Restoring overwrites the configuration files contained in the archive; files not present in the archive are left unchanged. Active sessions are not affected.
backup.restoreConfirm: Restore {name}? This overwrites the configuration files contained in the archive and reloads them. Active sessions are not affected. If the archive is older than the current admin key, you could lock yourself out.
backup.restoreFileConfirm: Restore from {name}? This overwrites the configuration files contained in the archive and reloads them. Active sessions are not affected.

lab.heading: App Laboratory
lab.help: Create a custom app from an installed base app, or edit an existing one. "Launch & modify" opens a live session whose home directory is the app's home template — changes you make inside are saved into the template for all future sessions.
lab.baseDesc: The new app inherits the image and provider settings from the base application.
lab.sessionPlaceholder: The customization session will appear here. Launch one to modify the app's home directory template.
lab.pickBaseAndName: Pick a base application and an app name first.
lab.saveBeforeLaunchFailed: Failed to save app settings before launching.
lab.sessionRunning: Customization session running — changes to the home directory are written into the app's template.

homedirs.title: Home directories
homedirs.help: Create or delete your persistent home directories. New ones appear in the launch options and the Files view.
homedirs.none: No home directories yet — create one below.
homedirs.deleteConfirm: Delete home directory '{name}'? Its files will be removed.
homedirs.invalidName: Use letters, numbers, underscore, or hyphen only.

pinned.defaultBadgeTitle: Restored on every login and used across all apps
pinned.installFirst: Install an app first to save a preset.
pinned.saveHelp: Save the current launch options as a reusable preset tied to an app. Re-apply it later from the Pinned list.
pinned.defaultHint: Your default preset is restored on every login and its launch options (GPU, home directory, language, …) are used across all apps, not just the one it was saved for. Only one preset can be your default.
